saints.name: St. Denis and Companions
saints.title: Bishop and Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: The first bishop of Paris, martyred with his companions and honoured as an apostle of Gaul…
biography: According to the earliest tradition Denis was sent from Rome by Pope Fabian about the middle of the third century to restore the Church of Gaul after the Decian persecution. Settling on an island in the Seine with the priest Rusticus and the deacon Eleutherius, he built a church, preached fearlessly, and is venerated as the first bishop of Paris.

Arrested with his two companions by the governor Fescenninus Sisinnius, the three were beheaded, in the tradition under the emperor Valerian about the year 258, on the hill north of the city afterward called Montmartre, a name long explained as the mount of the martyrs. A matron named Catulla buried them, and a shrine rose over their graves.

A later legend made Denis a cephalophore, rising after his execution to carry his own head, and it is from the manner of his death that he is invoked against headaches. The abbey of Saint-Denis, enriched by King Dagobert and the burial place of the kings of France, made him a national patron, of Paris and of the whole realm.
saints.knownFor: First bishop of Paris and martyr of Gaul.
